clue.text: Classes acting groups broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is put out over the air, so it is the spoken sound of the word that counts

parts.note: the companies of actors in plays are their casts

explanation.surface: Classes of theatre troupes are being put out on the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary social ranks, as in the Indian system, are classes in the strict sense of fixed strata.

clue.text: Grasping female I rejected, up-market sort

indicators.note: something grasping another piece holds it inside

parts.note: something up-market is classy

indicators.note: rejected things are turned back, so these letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A greedy woman, turned down by a posh type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like a noun meaning type; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To classify things is to arrange them into categories, which is to sort them.

clue.text: Rugby player and son getting cold drinks?

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
C is the tap abbreviation for cold
rum and a half (a half-pint of beer) are two drinks

explanation.surface: A rugby player and his boy getting chilled drinks after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: A half is British pub talk for half a pint of beer. A scrum half is the rugby player who feeds the ball into the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrum half is a specific position in a rugby team, so this is an example of a player.

clue.text: Top four sections fallen from fence? Go to get fencing tool!

indicators.note: losing the top four sections means the first four letters drop away

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to urinate, to pee

explanation.surface: A garden fence has collapsed; fetch a repair tool!
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' and 'fencing tool' suggest garden repairs; the tool is a sword for the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword used in the sport of fencing, with a stiff blade, is a fencer's weapon.

clue.text: Massive mistake if plaice presented badly

indicators.note: a dish served up badly is in a mess, so the letters of these words come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A chef's disaster: the fish dish was plated so badly it counts as a huge blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Internet slang for a spectacular, humiliating blunder; 'massive' matches the epic scale.

clue.text: I head back to tuck into vegetable bloomer

indicators.note: to tuck one thing into another puts it inside

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: I head back to eat a vegetable and make an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, or a British loaf; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plant grown for its flowers, so literally something that blooms.

clue.text: Am scared, so mixing some drinks

indicators.note: mixing something stirs it up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: I'm frightened, so I make a few cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla-flavoured fizzy soft drinks, so these are an example of drinks.

clue.text: Donkey going around motorway is wrong

indicators.note: something going around another piece encloses it

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A donkey wandering about on a motorway is not right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is out of order or faulty, so not right.

clue.text: Lacking bit of custom, shutting down

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: closing a door is shutting it

indicators.note: a bit of a word is here its opening letter

explanation.surface: A shop with too few customers is closing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shutting down' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'down' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is down is behind on the score, which is to say not winning.

clue.text: Shooting party worker hit by the Queen

parts.note: to beat is to hit
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A member of a shoot gets struck by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: On a British game shoot, the person who drives birds from cover towards the guns has this job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone employed to flush game from cover on a shoot is a hired helper there.

clue.text: Meet with anger, after scrapping Concord

indicators.note: after a scrap, or fight, things are knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Facing fury, and then a fight, before finally reaching peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concord' could be the aircraft or the town, but here it simply means harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Concord is harmony between parties, a state of being in accord with one another.

clue.text: In retreat, the enemy has small issues

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes backwards, so the word for the enemy is read in reverse

parts.note: 'time is the enemy' is a saying, so crosswords use the phrase for TIME
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A military report: the foe is falling back and has minor problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issues' looks like a noun (problems) but is a verb: sends out.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something, such as a statement or a signal, is to send it out or give it off.

clue.text: A few could be problem in hearing

indicators.note: what is heard is the spoken word, so a word that sounds alike is wanted

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem set in school

explanation.surface: A handful of people might have trouble with their ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a determiner, the word means an unspecified small number, a few.

clue.text: One working in rock moans notes in wrong order

indicators.note: items put in the wrong order are rearranged, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A rock musician groans out the notes of the song in the wrong order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working in rock' suggests a rock band; it means someone who carves stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who cuts, dresses and lays stone is literally a worker in rock.

clue.text: Courtesy is not messing around with sleep

indicators.note: letters messed around are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Good manners don't include fooling about with your nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtesy and good manners are synonyms for considerate behaviour.

clue.text: Having swilled drop of Lambrusco, go for taste

indicators.note: having swilled a drink means having taken it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to go for something is to favour it

indicators.note: a drop of the wine is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A wine-tasting: after swirling a little Lambrusco, try it for flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste and flavour are synonyms for the quality a food or drink has on the palate.

clue.text: Jacket, cardigan or a kid's clothes

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so these words wrap round the answer, which is concealed inside them

explanation.surface: A list of garments: a jacket, a cardigan, or a child's things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun in the list of garments; it is the verb, meaning covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded waterproof coat is a type of jacket.

clue.text: This might be the reason one can't get off Madeira

definitions.text: This might be the reason one can't get off Madeira

parts.words: This might be the reason one can't get off Madeira
parts.note: Madeira is an island, but also a fortified wine: being hooked on the drink is why you cannot give it up

explanation.surface: A traveller stuck on the Portuguese island wonders why.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependency on a substance, such as a fortified wine, keeps one from giving it up.

clue.text: What might fill worker and queen with worry?

definitions.text: What might fill worker and queen with worry?

indicators.note: filling means putting something inside another piece

parts.note: a worker is a kind of ant
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for a queen
to eat at someone, as in what's eating you, is to worry them

explanation.surface: Which creature would terrify a colony's worker and queen ants?
explanation.definitionFit: A mammal that feeds on ants and termites would be a terror to an ant colony.

clue.text: Declare commitment to a fine company

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Pledging loyalty to a good business.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm a belief or support is to state it publicly and firmly, pledging oneself to it.

clue.text: Ghastly taxi drawn by horse

indicators.note: a carriage drawn by a horse is held within its harness, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned horse-drawn cab, grim as something from Victorian horror.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gruesome, dwelling on death and horror, is ghastly.

clue.text: A musical group performing in dump

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
a performer is on, onstage

explanation.surface: A band playing a gig in a grotty venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dump' looks like a noun for a squalid place; it is the verb, to leave behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump someone or something is to desert or discard them.

clue.text: A flipping smack around priest's head shocks

indicators.note: going around another piece means enclosing it
flipping something turns it over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a slap is a smack

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A flaming slap given to a priest's head is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to horrify or dismay them.

clue.text: Consumes too much trash with geeks on occasion

parts.note: to bin something is to trash it

indicators.note: only on occasion means every other letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone overindulges in junk while hanging out with nerds now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on a spree of overindulgence in food or drink is to overconsume.

clue.text: Drunk spun on ice alarmingly close to falls

indicators.note: something going alarmingly is out of control, so these letters are mixed up
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A skater whirls on the ice, worryingly near to falling over.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in one's cups is an idiom for being intoxicated.

clue.text: Old academic describing European cinema

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so this piece goes around another

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: An elderly professor talking about a European film house.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known British chain of picture houses, so the name serves as a cinema.

clue.text: Long facial hair, but shaven off at front

indicators.note: shaving the front off loses the first letter

parts.note: a tache is short for a moustache

explanation.surface: A long moustache, but the front bit has been clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the hair; it is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn or pine for it.

clue.text: One little dog going up mountainous island

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
lab is a shortened name for a Labrador dog

explanation.surface: A single small dog climbing a hilly island.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indonesian island with volcanic peaks, so it fits as a hilly isle.

clue.text: Curt welcome baffles British diver

indicators.note: a baffle is a screen that encloses, so one piece surrounds the other
curt suggests cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to greet someone is to welcome them

explanation.surface: A terse hello puzzles a Brit going underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A water bird that dives for food under the surface, so a diver in the birdwatching sense.

clue.text: One makes song and dance at receiving insult

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: something receiving another piece takes it inside

parts.note: to dis is slang for to insult

explanation.surface: Someone makes a great fuss on being slighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'song and dance' reads as a fuss, but the definition stops at 'song'.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer or singer of ballads is someone whose work is producing songs.

clue.text: Menacing woman with habit seen outside home

indicators.note: something seen outside another surrounds it

parts.note: a nun wears a habit and is called Sister
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A threatening nun is spotted outside a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Something threatening, suggesting harm to come, is ominous or evil-seeming.

clue.text: Dutch leader having exclusive meal

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: an inner circle is an exclusive one

explanation.surface: The Dutch prime minister has a private meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The main meal of the day is a particular kind of meal.
